claims.text: NOAA (4 August 2026), on its GOES-West satellite smoke-monitoring coverage of the Pacific Northwest fires: "Hundreds of thousands of acres of land have been scorched so far by dozens of wildfires across the Pacific Northwest region, and many remain minimally contained. The fires have degraded air quality and caused evacuations of tens of thousands of people across Washington and Idaho."

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Washington State
claims.text: Office of the Governor of Washington State (4 August 2026): announces that President Trump approved a federal emergency declaration for Washington's wildfires, covering Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens and Yakima counties and the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation, the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, and the Spokane Tribe of Indians; Governor Ferguson: "The declaration allows our federal partners to mobilize their resources and personnel to support our response," including support for "evacuating and providing emergency shelters for people who are displaced by the wildfires," "emergency food and water, search and rescue operations and more." This followed Governor Ferguson's own statewide wildfire emergency proclamation of 1 August 2026. No casualty, structure-loss, or acreage figures are given in this release.

InciWeb's Sinlahekin Fire page, updated Friday, August 28, 2026 at 12:28 AM Pacific time, records the fire at 163,001 acres (up from 155,491 on 25 August) with containment at 49% (down from 56%) and 1,636 personnel assigned; the northwest portion showed extreme fire behavior -- crowning, uphill runs, torching and spotting -- with the fire spotting across 14 Mile Road despite firefighter efforts, under a Red Flag Warning for extremely dry fuels combined with increasing winds and unstable conditions; crews were establishing contingency lines toward Chopaka Mountain and strengthening containment along the eastern and southern edges, with estimated full containment still 31 August 2026.

InciWeb's Sinlahekin Fire page, updated Friday, August 28, 2026 at 9:10 PM Pacific time, records the fire at 166,216 acres (up from 163,001 on 28 August morning update) and still 49% contained, with 1,570 personnel assigned; fire behavior remains extreme with uphill runs, torching and spotting concentrated on the northwest side, and the outlook anticipates cooler temperatures and higher humidity moderating behavior over the next 72+ hours with little further growth expected, though interior heat persists. No specific full-containment date is given in this update.

InciWeb's Sinlahekin Fire page, updated Sunday, August 30, 2026 at 9:49 PM Pacific time, records the fire at 166,413 acres (up from 166,216 on 28 August) with 'Percent of Perimeter Contained: 40%' (down from 49%) and 1,684 personnel assigned; overnight crews observed 'excellent recoveries (70% to 100%)' with moist fuels limiting activity to smoldering and consuming heavy fuels, and 24-48 hour projections anticipate no fire spread with only limited creeping possible in large woody fuels. A warming, drying trend continues through Tuesday before an approaching cold front brings southerly winds, rain chances and higher humidity for the remainder of the week.

claims.text: On 7 August 2026 the US Department of Health and Human Services approved Governor Ferguson's request to declare a federal Public Health Emergency in response to the Eastern Washington wildfires, covering the same six counties (Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Yakima) and three tribal nations (Yakama Nation, Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, Spokane Tribe of Indians) already covered by the 4 August 2026 federal emergency declaration.

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Washington State
claims.text: On 7 August 2026, Governor Bob Ferguson's office announced that the US Department of Health and Human Services approved his request to declare a Public Health Emergency for the wildfire-affected areas of Eastern Washington -- Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens and Yakima counties, plus the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation, the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, and the Spokane Tribe of Indians. This is a second, stacked federal declaration alongside the major disaster/emergency declaration Washington received on 4 August 2026. No death or displacement figures have been published on an allowlisted source.

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Washington State
claims.text: On 10 August 2026, Governor Bob Ferguson signed an emergency proclamation suspending numerous state laws to help those affected by the wildfires, now covering Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Douglas and Yakima counties plus the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation, the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, and the Spokane Tribe of Indians (adding Douglas County to the area covered by the 4 August federal emergency declaration). The Governor's office states: "My emergency proclamation waives and suspends numerous state laws so that help can move quickly," and the proclamation suspends disaster cash assistance eligibility requirements, personal document replacement fees, professional license renewal deadlines, unemployment benefit waiting periods and job-search requirements, a two-week limitation on eviction-related actions, healthcare provider licensing and supervision requirements, hospital and pharmacy licensing restrictions, and adult family home/assisted living facility capacity limitations, and waives late fees for employers unable to file or pay second-quarter 2026 taxes because of the wildfires. No death toll, injury count, acreage, containment, or displacement figures are given in this release.

description: Dozens of wildfires broke out across the Pacific Northwest in late July and early August 2026, burning hundreds of thousands of acres and forcing evacuations of tens of thousands of people across eastern Washington State and into Idaho. Governor Bob Ferguson proclaimed a statewide wildfire emergency on 1 August, and a federal emergency declaration approved on 4 August 2026 covers six counties plus the Yakama Nation, the Colville Reservation and the Spokane Tribe of Indians; the governor's office reports over 1,000 fires and approximately 425,000 acres burned statewide, the highest acreage since 2021, with 110 National Guard members activated. The Sinlahekin Fire, the state's largest, had grown to 166,413 acres and was 40% contained as of 30 August 2026, with 1,684 personnel assigned; overnight crews reported excellent fuel-moisture recovery and smoldering-only activity, and short-term projections anticipate no further fire spread as cooler, more humid conditions with rain chances move in behind an approaching cold front. No confirmed death toll or structure-loss count has been published for the emergency as a whole.

impact.summary: The Sinlahekin Fire, the state's largest, started by a lightning strike on 26 July 2026 about 12 miles west of Tonasket and had grown to 166,413 acres at 40% containment as of the evening of 30 August 2026, with 1,684 personnel assigned; overnight crews observed excellent fuel-moisture recovery (70-100%) limiting fire activity to smoldering and consumption of heavy fuels, and 24-48 hour projections anticipate no further fire spread. A warming, drying trend continues through Tuesday before an approaching cold front brings southerly winds, rain chances and higher humidity for the rest of the week. Statewide, the governor's office reports over 1,000 fires and approximately 425,000 acres burned, the highest acreage since 2021, with 200,000+ acres actively burning across 12 large fires at the emergency's height, 110 National Guard members activated and 13 State Fire Marshal task forces mobilized. Federal emergency and Public Health Emergency declarations cover six counties and three tribal nations; no confirmed death toll or structure-loss figure has been published.
